question: Koplik spots — tiny white lesions on the buccal mucosa opposite the lower molars — are pathognomonic of measles and appear before the characteristic maculopapular rash.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is TRUE. Koplik spots are small white lesions on the buccal mucosa opposite the lower molars. They are pathognomonic of measles and appear during the prodrome (along with the 3 C's: coryza, cough, conjunctivitis), 1–2 days BEFORE the cephalocaudal maculopapular rash erupts.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Koplik spots are pathognomonic of measles — they appear 1–2 days before the maculopapular rash erupts (during the prodrome phase of 3 C's: coryza, cough, conjunctivitis). Their presence confirms measles clinically and is an important early diagnostic sign before the rash appears.
